deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no mathematics: no formulas, no derivations, and no computations. It is a page of Riemann's epistemological and natural-philosophical drafts (the 'Erkenntnisstheoretisches' section; the next page begins 'III Naturphilosophie. 1. Molecularmechanik'). Its content, restated:

(a) End of a preceding argument about refining concepts. Suppose an element of light (e.g. a light-ether element) is replaced by a complex of finer elements. Light's properties would then follow partly from simpler properties of those elements and partly from how they are combined, so they become partly comprehensible. Our insight into the connection of things would grow. The point appears to be that the earlier conception would not thereby have to be declared false; the reading is uncertain.

(b) 'II. From what is the connection of things to be found?' Answer: 'from the connection of the phenomena.' What is given is the distribution of sense-objects in definite spatial and temporal relations. The qualities of sensation (colour, sound, smell, taste, warmth, cold) belong only to our sensation. Hence the connection of things must be read off from relations of magnitude (Grössenverhältnisse):
- spatial and temporal relations;
- intensity relations of the sensory marks and of their qualitative differences.
Reflection on how these magnitude-relations hang together must yield knowledge of the connection of things. This is a programmatic statement that natural science is quantitative.

(c) 'Causalität', four numbered theses:
- I. If an agent strives to effect something, this must be determined by the concept of the agent; its action depends only on its own nature.
- II. This condition is met if the agent strives to preserve or restore itself.
- III. Such striving is unthinkable for a thing or being (there are no degrees of being). It is possible only for a state or relation, because striving to preserve something presupposes graded deviations from it. Under competing strivings the agent is preserved only 'as far as possible'.
- IV. Such an action of a state can act only on things capable of the same state. On which of them it acts, and whether at all, cannot be inferred from the concept of the agent.

Footnote *): these theses hold only if the action is ascribed to a simple real ground. If two things a and b are brought into connection by an external ground, a consequence c can be attached either to the connectedness itself or to the change of each. The simplest assumption is that c attaches to the connectedness. Then comes a self-critical remark that the error of this line of reasoning lies in positing thesis I without (justifying) it. In red ink in the margin: 'Nicht Sache der Logik' (not a matter of logic).

(d) Critique of Kant. Kant rightly saw that existence and causality are not analytic (cannot be obtained by dissecting a concept) and must come from experience. But making causality an a priori form, a mere rule of temporal succession, 'throws the baby out with the bathwater'. We take causal relations from experience but must correct and complete our grasp of them by reflection.

Relevance to the mathematics: thesis III ('preserved only as far as possible' when strivings conflict) is the metaphysical motivation for the next page. There Newton's law is recast as a minimum principle in the style of Gauss's least constraint. Opposing tendencies balance so that a sum of quantities each cause strives to keep small becomes a minimum. That modelling idea is the only link to mathematics.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible; the page has no computations.
Riemann himself flags a logical weakness: thesis I is asserted but not justified ('Ihr Fehler besteht darin, daß man den Satz hinstellt ... diesen Satz aber nicht, ...').
Philosophically, the step from 'no degrees of being' to 'every agent is a state or relation' is asserted rather than argued.
The reading of Kant as reducing causality to a rule under which any perception could be linked with any other as effect is a contestable caricature of the Second Analogy.

results.what: Thesis that the connection of things must be inferred solely from relations of magnitude: spatial, temporal, and intensity relations. Secondary qualities are treated as subjective.
results.modern_name: Primary/secondary quality distinction; quantitative (mathematical) conception of physics
results.usually_credited_to: Galileo, Locke; in the 19th century Helmholtz and others

results.what: Causal agent as a state or relation striving to preserve or restore itself, realised only 'as far as possible' when strivings conflict. This motivates minimum principles in mechanics.
results.modern_name: Metaphysical motivation for extremal/variational principles (cf. Gauss's principle of least constraint)
results.usually_credited_to: Leibniz/Maupertuis (metaphysics of extremal principles); Gauss 1829 (least constraint); Herbart's influence on Riemann

results.what: Critique of Kant's a priori causality ('das Kind mit dem Bade ausschütten')

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely philosophical. It belongs to Riemann's natural-philosophy fragments, parts of which were published by Weber and Dedekind in the Gesammelte Werke ('Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts'), and its themes are known Riemann/Herbart themes. The Causality theses and the Kant critique may be less well known in detail. Even so, they contain no mathematics and nothing that would change attributions.
transcription_corrections: First paragraph, final clause: the sense and handwriting suggest something like 'so würde dadurch zwar unsere Einsicht in den Zusammenhang der Dinge [erweitert], aber ohne daß die frühere Auffassung für falsch erklärt werden müßte'. The transcribed 'aber eben dadurch[?] die frühere Auffassung für falsch erklärt werden müßte' is ungrammatical and likely misread (uncertain).
'das Licht selbst sein[?] Wesen der Beschreibung' is doubtful; the image does not clearly support 'Wesen der Beschreibung' (uncertain, leave flagged).
'den inneren[?] Zusammenhang dieser Grössenverhältnisse': the word before 'Zusammenhang' is unclear in the image; keep it flagged.
The red marginal note 'Nicht Sache der Logik[?]' is written vertically beside the footnote; its reading is plausible but uncertain.
